application_type: multi-image visual reasoning over charts, documents and photographs
daily_active_users_u_reason: (U) this campaign was specified directly in concurrent users, not DAU
peak_to_mean_u_reason: (U) not applicable; CCU is already the peak figure
requests_per_session_u_reason: (U) the ladder issues independent requests rather than multi-turn sessions, so no per-session request count was declared
video_seconds_per_request_u_reason: (U) no video is sent; this corpus is images only
reasoning_share_u_reason: (U) reasoning_share is meaningful only for a mixed workload; no record in this corpus carries a reasoning turn, so the run is uniformly non-thinking

notes.where_the_media_numbers_come_from: images_per_request is exact over the corpus -- 13,644 images across 3,256 records, from the reader's own media_shape, not from the corpus card. media_tokens_per_request is measured against this server: 300 draws were rendered through the same corpus object the ladder uses and sent twice each, once with the image parts and once with the text part alone, and the difference is the media's cost with the chat template held constant. Over those draws the media cost 265.23 tokens per image (weighted by image, spread 252 to 276.5 per request -- the same price model.image_tokens_fixed carries as the integer 265, measured there over 24 synthetic resolutions at 265.1 unweighted), and 4.1904 times that is the 1111.5 declared here. The declaration deliberately uses the corpus-wide image count rather than the sample's 4.2767, because the count is exact and the per-image price is what needed measuring; the direct sample mean was 1134.3, and the difference is the sample drawing slightly image-heavy records. This is a pre-run declaration, so the run's own prompt-token total is an independent check on it, which is the point of media_token_cap_check.
notes.input_tokens_per_request_is_the_text_tha: 33.5 tokens, measured the same way: the mean server-reported prompt_tokens for the text part alone, chat template included. It is small because these prompts are questions about the images rather than passages -- the shortest was 19 tokens and the longest 101. Two consequences worth stating. The workload is roughly 97 percent media by prompt token, so anything that changes the image price moves the whole prefill and KV story, and this is the workload where the difference between the checkpoint's declared 280 tokens per image and the measured 265 is not a rounding argument. And a text-only comparison against ../gb200-gemma4-31b-tp1/ is not like for like on the text side either: that campaign declared 1,500 synthetic input tokens, so the two runs share a KV pool and a model and nothing else about the prompt.
notes.avg_context_tokens_composition: 1395.0 is 33.5 text plus 1111.5 media plus half of the 500 output tokens, tagged M because the prompt side is server-measured rather than forecast. The output half is the residency convention every ASCEP report uses -- a request holds its generated tokens for on average half the generation -- and is a model, not a measurement; it is stated here so a reader does not read the M as covering all three terms.
notes.the_resolution_mix_is_truncated_and_the_: This corpus has 11,916 distinct resolutions across its 13,644 images: almost every image is its own resolution, because the images are real charts, scanned pages and photographs rather than a curated set. The 32 rows above are the most common, and they cover 4.61 percent of the images. So the fractions sum to 0.046, not to 1, and the schema's SHOULD is knowingly not met -- listing every row would be a 700 KB workload declaration that no operator can transcribe or check. The alternative of reporting a mean resolution is worse, since the field exists precisely because a mean hides the spread. What is missing is a place to declare the residual: the bench's media_shape now reports image_resolution_mix_listed_share and image_resolution_mix_distinct alongside the mix, and the workload schema has no matching field, so on this corpus the two disagree about how complete the mix is and only the prose says which is right. That is a protocol gap this campaign found, recorded here rather than patched by inventing a field in an example.
notes.the_mix_matters_less_on_this_model_than_: The field's description warns that on a dynamic-resolution model a single mean resolution hides a tenfold token spread. On this model it hides almost nothing: the measured cost is 252 to 276.5 tokens per image over the whole corpus, a spread of under 10 percent, because Gemma-4 fits every image to the same 280-token grid budget and only the aspect ratio moves the count. The mix is still declared because it is the input a reader needs to price the same corpus on a model that does scale with pixels, and this bundle is meant to be compared against exactly such a run.
notes.concurrent_users_and_duty_cycle_are_inhe: 200 users at a 0.25 duty cycle and 15 tokens per second per user are carried over unchanged from the text campaign so the two reports differ only in what the prompts contain. They describe a hypothetical deployment, not this corpus, and nothing in the ladder measures them.
